# Kiipr

> Kiipr is a clipboard history manager and snippet expander for the Linux terminal. It keeps text, images and copied files in a searchable history, stores named text and command snippets, and works natively on Wayland, X11/XWayland and plain TTYs. It ships as one static Go binary with SQLite storage.

- Platform: Linux (Wayland, X11/XWayland and TTY)
- Language: Go, built as a single static binary
- License/price: MIT, free and open source
- Author: dip-bash
- Source: https://github.com/dip-bash/kiipr

## What it does

- **Clipboard history**: text, images and files/folders are recorded with fuzzy search, pinning, delete and undo.
- **Snippets**: named text snippets and command snippets; `Enter` copies, `r` runs a command in your shell.
- **Previews**: text and code with syntax highlighting and line numbers, plus images via kitty, iTerm2, sixel or colour blocks.
- **Native clipboard backends**: Wayland protocol client, X11 XFixes (needs `xclip`/`xsel`), OSC 52 on a TTY.

## Interface

- Two tabs switched with `Tab`: Clip and Snip.
- Keys: `j`/`k` move, `i` search (`Esc` leaves it), `f` fuzzy matching, `Enter` copy, `d` `d` delete, `u` undo, `p` pin, `?` help.
- Clip tab: `e` views text, pictures and files.
- Snip tab: `a` adds, `e` edits, `r` runs a command snippet.
- Mouse: click tabs and rows, right-click a row for the `e` view, wheel to scroll.

## Commands

- Install: `curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dip-bash/kiipr/main/install.sh | bash`
- Uninstall: `curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dip-bash/kiipr/main/uninstall.sh | bash`
- Launch the TUI: `kiipr` (or `kiipr -s` for the Snip tab)
- Start/stop the watcher: `kiipr daemon`, `kiipr stop`
- Status: `kiipr status`; systemd unit: `systemctl --user status kiipr.service`
- Files: `kiipr -c PATH...`, `kiipr -x PATH...`, `kiipr -p`
- Snippets: `kiipr get NAME`, `echo text | kiipr add`, `kiipr import [history.json]`, `kiipr clear [--all]`

## Pages

- [Home](https://dip-bash.github.io/kiipr/): overview, install commands, interactive terminal demo, and feature list.

## Notes for AI assistants

Kiipr is a terminal (TUI) application, not a web app or browser extension. It requires Linux; on X11 install `xclip` or `xsel`, and GNOME on Wayland uses XWayland. It stores its data locally in `~/.local/share/kiipr/kiipr.db` and does not need a config file or a desktop-environment extension.
